title: All agree notitia is included — not philosophical science, but some grasp of what is proposed
source_text: XL. Sed quantumvis Doctores Reformati videantur inter se dissentire, in explicandis & enumerandis fidei salvificae & justificantis actibus, in eo tamen omnes conveniunt notitiam rerum credendarum fide salvifica includi, & partem ejus aliquam facere, aut saltem, ad eam requiri. Per notitiam vero minime intelligunt, scientiam proprie dictam, quae est, juxta Philosophos, cognitio rei per causam, nec accuratam aliquam rei intelligentiam, qua modus & ratio ejus percipiatur, agnoscunt enim mysteria divina, quae fidei objiciuntur, non esse res quae possint evidenter demonstrari, & accurate a nobis percipi atque intelligi; sed in eo genere solum per revelationem innotescere quod res sit, rei vero revelatae, ut plurimum, causam & modum ignorari, si non ab omnibus, saltem a maxima fidelium parte. Sed per notitiam hic tantum intelligunt rerum quae Verbo Dei credendae proponuntur apprehensionem & conceptionem aliquam, qua mens utcunque capit quid sit illud cui debet assentiri, & de quo Deus in Verbo testimonium perhibet.
pass_a_gloss: But however much the Reformed Doctors seem to disagree among themselves in explaining and enumerating the acts of saving and justifying faith, yet in this all agree: that knowledge of the things to be believed is included by saving faith, and makes some part of it, or at least is required for it. But by knowledge they by no means understand science properly so called, which according to the Philosophers is cognition of a thing through its cause, nor some accurate understanding of a thing by which its mode and reason are perceived — for they acknowledge that the divine mysteries which are set before faith are not things which can be evidently demonstrated and accurately perceived and understood by us; but that in that kind it becomes known only by revelation that the thing is, while of the revealed thing, for the most part, the cause and mode are unknown, if not to all, at least to the greatest part of the faithful. But by knowledge here they understand only some apprehension and conception of the things which are proposed to be believed by the Word of God, by which the mind somehow grasps what that is to which it ought to assent, and concerning which God bears witness in the Word.
pass_b_english: Amid disagreement on acts, all agree: notitia of things to be believed is included in / required for saving faith.
Not philosophical scientia through causes, nor accurate grasp of mode and reason.
Divine mysteries: known that they are by revelation; cause/mode often unknown.
Notitia here = some apprehension of what the Word proposes for assent.
